newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest grains futures little changed in slow mkt.
newsitem.headline: Budapest grains futures little changed in slow mkt.

text.p: Grains futures prices on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) were little changed on Thursday in minimal turnover, traders said.
Total turnover was a meagre 444 lots or 238 million forints, almost the same as Wednesday's 447 lots or 221 million forints.
Milling wheat futures finished 10 to 280 forints per tonne lower for maturities until May 1998, which traders said was due to the closing of open selling positions.
"There was some liquidation after the (agriculture) ministry's announcement of wheat quality on Wednesday," said Balazs Orban of Agrograin.
The Ministry said that while the quality of the milling wheat crop was lowered by persistent rains during harvesting, the damage was less than sources outside the ministry had suggested.
However, Orban said the market did not fully subscribe to the ministry's opinion and a number of other sources, including shipping and trading companies, were more pessimistic.
"Prices closed only slightly lower and that shows a strong support at current levels," he said.
Milling wheat prices for the 1997 crop settled at between 28,030 forints per tonne for September and 33,620 for May.
Feed wheat futures finished slightly lower in what Orban said was an upward correction, but he added that there was scope for further downward movement.
"We have heard of spot deals for shipments to South Korea at $129 CIF," he said. That price was below current BCE prices.
September feed wheat finished at 17,000 forints, up 200, December at 18,750, up 120, and May at 20,160, up 10.

Feed barley dropped the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne for all but the September maturity but Orban said the move was inconsequential due to the small number of contracts and the fact that barley had an illiquid market.
